pr_title: Data: ShadowRoot support listen events & data get/set
pr_body:
### Summary ###
<!--
Describe what this PR does. All but trivial changes (e.g. typos)
should start with an issue. Mention the issue number here.
-->
JQuery adds constraints, do not allow add data and add event listen to non-elements, see [bugs-8335](https://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/8335)

And ShadowRoot elements have `nodeType === 11`

But ShadowRoot elements are supported only on modern browsers, so this fix (owner.nodeType === 11 && owner.host) can be discussed here

Fixes [gh-4317](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues/4317) [gh-4418](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues/4418)

issue_context.title: Is not possible to listen events on ShadowRoot
issue_context.body:
### Description ### When trying to listen events on a ShadowRoot element using `on`, the handler is not fired. The native addEventListener works Minimal example: ```javascript const el = $("#test")[0]; el.attachShadow({ mode: "open" }); el.shadowRoot.innerHTML = `
Inner content
`; $(el.shadowRoot).on("click", ".inner", () => { console.log("jquery - shadow inner clicked"); }); ``` The issue is that the element data returned by dataPriv is always empty because of [this check](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/master/src/data/var/acceptData.js#L16) ShadowRoot elements have nodeType === 11 The [issue](https://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/8335) [pointed](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/e743cbd28553267f955f71ea7248377915613fd9/src/data/Data.js#L28) as reason for the check seems not valid for ShadowRoot elements which are supported only on modern browsers So, changing the check for ```javascript return owner.nodeType === 1 || owner.nodeType === 9 || owner.nodeType === 11 || !( +owner.nodeType ); ``` should work ### Link to test case ### https://codepen.io/blikblum/pen/QogVgO?editors=1111
comments: I agree with the bug but not the solution. We shouldn't be adding event listeners to any `nodeType===11` which includes `DocumentFragment`. For example, if a jQuery event handler was attached to a `DocumentFragment` and the DF was later inserted in to the document, we wouldn't clean up internal data structures.

BTW: the underlying issue is not specific for events. It also affects [setting data](https://codepen.io/blikblum/pen/zbMpaW?editors=1111).

AFAICS the memory leak that prevented attaching data to non elements does not occurs with current implementation of jQuery and >= IE8, so should not be a problem.

If attaching to `DocumentFragment` is still a concern, should be acceptable a more specific check to restrict to `ShadowRoot`?

Something like:
```javascript
return owner.nodeType === 1 || owner.nodeType === 9 || (owner.nodeType === 11 && owner.host) || !( +owner.nodeType );
```
Hi @extempl, a proposed solution is above. Would you like to submit a pull request?

review_comments: @jquery/core do you remember the reasons we don't allow data on document fragments? Or in general, what are the reasons to maintain any restrictions? In the past there were issues with host objects, browser plugins, etc., but plugins went away and many of these problems got smoothed out.
